races.name: Lay & Wheeler Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Hallgarten Wines Jockey Club Partner Handicap

runners_data.name: Change Sings
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's six-year-old is a consistent prominent racer at this trip, with three places in four runs on Good ground at six furlongs, and Charles Bishop's positive booking adds confidence; 10 days since last run is ideal freshness.

runners_data.name: Sixtygeesbaby
runners_data.note: Tudhope takes over for O'Meara's hold-up specialist, who showed a clear best-of-going profile on Good and ran well fresh 40 days back; the tongue-tie is retained and his two wins at six furlongs both came from off the pace on Good ground.

runners_data.name: Fiscal Policy
runners_data.note: Mrs Carr's consistent seven-year-old has a fine recent record showing 1-2-2-3 in his last five, all on Good at six furlongs, making him a significant threat on form — but he is a natural pace-seeker who will find himself shuffled into a midfield berth he doesn't naturally want, tempering how likely he is to fully deliver.

runners_data.name: Angel Gabriel
runners_data.note: Beckett's lightly-raced three-year-old is the key pace-setter and, critically, faces no genuine rival for the lead; 192 days off the track is the one notable query, though his two all-weather runs were sharp and Rossa Ryan's booking suggests he is fit enough to do a job.

runners_data.name: Sierra Sands
runners_data.note: Showed a 1-4-10 profile at six to seven furlongs on Good ground, and Ryan Moore's experience is a significant booking for Dunlop's colt — but he is a genuinely prominent-minded horse who will be shuffled back by the volume of pace in this field, racing outside his comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Fresh Fade
runners_data.note: Attwater's lightly-weighted three-year-old is a true hold-up type whose best Newmarket effort was a sixth in a similar race; 33 days off is adequate freshness, but the best form figures in similar conditions (11/13) are modest and he needs the pace to really flow to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Ice Cube
runners_data.note: Spencer's juvenile is the lowest-rated runner (OR 61) and is a genuine hold-up horse who has been mapped to a midfield position because the rear is crowded — he is essentially racing out of role on an already tall task; the headgear change to hood may help focus, but this looks a stiff ask off just 20 days.

runners_data.name: Secret History
runners_data.note: Walker's progressive three-year-old arrives in the best recent form in the field — 1-1-2 in his last three — and Oisin Murphy's booking is the most eye-catching in the race; four of his five runs have been at seven furlongs to a mile, so dropping to six on Good is the question, though his win at six furlongs at Southwell showed he handles the shorter trip.

races.paceDynamic: Angel Gabriel is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the off on Good ground at Newmarket's straight six. Change Sings and Secret History will push forward to sit prominently just behind, creating a compressed early order rather than a breakneck pace. This field contains more prominent-minded types than the map can accommodate — Sierra Sands and Fiscal Policy are natural pace-seekers who will be squeezed into a midfield role they do not naturally suit, meaning their chance is conditioned on a scenario that is harder for them to execute. A single, unhurried front-runner on Good ground over six furlongs at Newmarket typically sets up a race for those racing prominently in behind — horses with enough early pace to track the leader but the cruising speed to sustain it, rather than pure hold-up closers who will need a searching gallop to deliver their finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Angel Gabriel Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Angel Gabriel bowls along uncontested and the pace stays honest but never truly severe, rewarding those travelling smoothly in behind.
scenarios.body: If Angel Gabriel bowls along uncontested and the pace stays honest but never truly severe, rewarding those travelling smoothly in behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Hold Produces Winner
scenarios.trigger: If Angel Gabriel's pace is just quick enough to string the field out but not fast enough to ensure dominance, those tracking prominent in first-run positions close him down.
scenarios.body: If Angel Gabriel's pace is just quick enough to string the field out but not fast enough to ensure dominance, those tracking prominent in first-run positions close him down.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steadied Pace Suits Held-Up Closer
scenarios.trigger: If Angel Gabriel crawls and the first two furlongs are unusually sedate, creating a bunched field that suddenly quickens, a genuine hold-up runner finishing fast could thread through.
scenarios.body: If Angel Gabriel crawls and the first two furlongs are unusually sedate, creating a bunched field that suddenly quickens, a genuine hold-up runner finishing fast could thread through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos Scrambles Race
scenarios.trigger: If jostling for position early forces Sierra Sands or Fiscal Policy to burn petrol disputing leads they were not mapped to contest, creating an unexpectedly strong pace.
scenarios.body: If jostling for position early forces Sierra Sands or Fiscal Policy to burn petrol disputing leads they were not mapped to contest, creating an unexpectedly strong pace.

watchPoints.text: Angel Gabriel's 192-day absence is the single biggest risk to the dominant scenario — watch the market and paddock closely, as any sign of ring-rustiness could unravel the entire pace map.

Sierra Sands and Fiscal Policy are genuine pace-seeking horses who cannot both get the position they want — monitor the early stalls for any scramble that could ignite a stronger-than-expected early gallop.
Secret History drops from seven furlongs to six and runs on turf for the first time — if he fails to settle or doesn't get the trip, Oisin Murphy's optimum race shape disappears quickly.
Sixtygeesbaby is the truest hold-up closer in the field but depends almost entirely on the pace being strong enough; if Angel Gabriel saunters, Tudhope may have no race to close into.

Change Sings has finished placed in three of four runs at this trip on Good ground this season but hasn't won in 15 starts — watch whether Bishop attempts to improve his position early to get closer to Angel Gabriel than the pace map currently suggests.

races.name: Empress Fillies' Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Beauty Box
runners_data.note: Three starts in, she has won over 6f Good and placed twice — a progressive sort for Tate whose unknown running style is a tactical wildcard; Clifford Lee will need to find her a position early in what is a busy race for pace.|

runners_data.name: Californian Angel
runners_data.note: Palmer's filly won her only race at OR=120 level and Cieren Fallon drops her in from hold-up to let the pace unfold in front of her; one run of form but that single outing on Good ground was encouraging.|

runners_data.name: Glorious Game
runners_data.note: Palmer's highest-rated runner and a front-runner by profile, but her sole victory came on Soft — the step up to Good is a flag worth monitoring, though Murphy is perfectly capable of making the running and controlling the tempo.|

runners_data.name: Havana Sprite
runners_data.note: Tate's pace-setter wants to lead just like her stablemate, and with only a 5f winning mark to her name this step to 6f with another confirmed front-runner in the field is a genuine concern; Crouch will need to commit from the start.|

runners_data.name: Margaret's Pearl
runners_data.note: Wearing a tongue-tie and hood, she won over 5f Good before finishing tenth last time — 41 days off and stepping up to Listed company is a big ask, though De Sousa gives her every chance from a prominent berth.|

runners_data.name: Motown Filly
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with OR=120 who ran second on Soft at 6f in her only start — Saffie Osborne gets the ride for Spencer and she represents a horse that could slot ideally just off a contested pace if she handles the better ground.|

runners_data.name: The Can Can Queen
runners_data.note: Johnston's filly has a win over today's 6f trip at Goodwood and McDonald is a booking worth respecting; she has form on Soft but her Good-ground record (2 from 3 in similar conditions) is solid for a horse rated OR=70.|

runners_data.name: What A Girl Wants
runners_data.note: De Foy's runner has run four times and finished placed three times, but that sole win record and a last run of just six days ago raises questions about freshness; David Egan will aim to cover her hold-up tendencies from mid-division.|

races.paceDynamic: Glorious Game and Havana Sprite both want to lead, and with Oisin Murphy and Hector Crouch in the saddle respectively, neither is likely to concede easily — this shapes as a genuinely contested early gallop over 6f on Good ground at Newmarket. The pressure between these two from the gates will stretch the field and set an honest, possibly brisk, tempo that burns through the field by the two-furlong pole. Margaret's Pearl and The Can Can Queen will slot in behind the pace-setters, while Californian Angel and What A Girl Wants will be doing their best work from further back. This race shape most favours prominent-to-hold-up types who can sit just off a contested lead and pick up the pieces when the two front-runners do battle — horses with a strong finishing effort over 6f on Good ground stand to benefit most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Burn Out
scenarios.trigger: If Glorious Game and Havana Sprite fight for supremacy from the gates and set a searching pace that softens both of them.
scenarios.body: If Glorious Game and Havana Sprite fight for supremacy from the gates and set a searching pace that softens both of them.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Glorious Game Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Glorious Game asserts natural dominance and Havana Sprite drops away early, allowing a clean, controlled lead.
scenarios.body: If Glorious Game asserts natural dominance and Havana Sprite drops away early, allowing a clean, controlled lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly fierce and the entire prominent group ties up inside the final furlong, opening the door for deep hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: If the pace is truly fierce and the entire prominent group ties up inside the final furlong, opening the door for deep hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Rail Runner
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent runner benefits from a split on the rail and avoids the traffic caused by the front-runner duel.
scenarios.body: If a prominent runner benefits from a split on the rail and avoids the traffic caused by the front-runner duel.

watchPoints.text: Glorious Game and Havana Sprite — watch the first two furlongs closely; if neither concedes the lead, a scorching early pace could compromise both and turn this race on its head for every other runner.

Glorious Game — her only win came on Soft ground; monitor market moves and early race behaviour to see if she handles the Good going, as a poor surface response could see Murphy ease her out of contention quickly.

Havana Sprite — stepping from 5f to 6f in a Listed race while also likely to be embroiled in a pace battle is a significant double-ask; if she weakens sharply after two furlongs, this is the trigger for the late-closer scenario.

Motown Filly — Saffie Osborne's booking on an OR=120 filly with only one run is intriguing; watch where she settles in running, as getting cover just off the contested lead suits her profile perfectly for a strong finish.

What A Girl Wants — only six days since her last run, which is notably short for a return to Listed level; watch her in the paddock and early in the race for any signs of staleness that could blunt her hold-up finish.

races.name: laywheeler.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Superposition
runners_data.note: Has a genuine course win over 7f Good and is well-suited to the straight track in a prominent role, though his recent history shows a sharp drop in form over 8f on Tapeta — returning to his optimum conditions here is the key angle.

runners_data.name: Dark Tornado
runners_data.note: Visored hold-up performer with a clean recent record on Good ground but has not threatened the frame in his last five starts, all over 7-8f Good; 6 days since last run is fresh, but his finishing position sequence of 5-8-8-7-8 is concerning.

runners_data.name: Darkness
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse with visor, Daniel Tudhope booking is positive, but 10 of his last 15 runs on Good have produced no better than a sixth — form string of 0-7-6-0-0 is alarming and he needs the pace to truly collapse to get involved.

runners_data.name: Nostrum
runners_data.note: Mark Appleby's hold-up horse was placed at 8f Good last time and has tactical speed, but his true rear-end style is squeezed out of position in this field — the redistribution means he will race closer than he wants, compromising his strongest weapon of a sustained late run.

runners_data.name: Philanthropist
runners_data.note: Fanshawe's 4-year-old won over this course and distance on Good and has genuine prominent speed, but with Northern Express controlling affairs from the front and other prominent types filling the early slots, Rossa Ryan will find it harder to secure his preferred berth than the form book suggests.

runners_data.name: Aalto
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's booking is always noteworthy but Aalto has finished no closer than seventh in his last five over 7f Good, and as a genuine hold-up horse nudged forward into midfield by the crowded rear, he is unlikely to produce the late flourish his style depends on.

runners_data.name: I Still Have Faith
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa partners this prominent-style mare who has placed three times in her last five but has not won; forced out of a natural front-tracking role by a busy prominent group, she may find herself racing in no-man's land between the leaders and closers.

runners_data.name: Silver Ghost
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes over on a 4-year-old with an excellent recent record at 7f Good (2nd, 3rd, placed in four of five course attempts) and the natural prominent style to sit just off Northern Express before delivering a clean challenge — 40 days off but the form profile is strong.

runners_data.name: Northern Express
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 96, the sole front-runner in the field, and proven at 7-9f on Good ground with a 13/15 sim-going strike rate; Sean Kirrane gets a simple tactical brief, though 126 days off is a question-mark and the STYLE_FIT tag slightly tempers confidence he will quicken away from rivals in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Mudbir
runners_data.note: Won twice last season at 7f Good and Gosden/Buick is a formidable combination; he has been freshened for 47 days and at OR 94 has class to burn, but the 22nd-place finish on his most recent 7f Good start is hard to ignore without clear explanation.

runners_data.name: Hawksbill
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne partners this 4-year-old who has 13 of 15 qualifying runs on Good, but returning from 111 days off with a recent form string of 0-5-0-6-0 offers little encouragement — needs a significant step forward to feature.

races.paceDynamic: Northern Express is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival able to challenge for the lead, he should bowl along at a sustainable, metronomic tempo through this flat 7f Newmarket straight. Silver Ghost, Superposition, and Mudbir are natural prominent types who will press into second and third berths, keeping the race honest without turning it into a scramble. The field actually holds more prominent and hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate — Philanthropist and I Still Have Faith are both genuine prominent racers who are unlikely to secure their preferred positions and will be forced wider or further back than ideal, while Nostrum and Aalto, true hold-up horses, are similarly squeezed toward midfield rather than settling at the true rear. A controlled, single-file pace at 7f on Good ground at Newmarket is a shape that classically suits horses racing prominently in the first three or four, able to pick off the front-runner in the final two furlongs without needing a sustained late sprint from deep — the prominent-to-midfield profile holds the clearest tactical advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Northern Express Dictates Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Express is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a relaxed, controlled tempo that saps the finish from hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: If Northern Express is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a relaxed, controlled tempo that saps the finish from hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is just quick enough that Northern Express ties up inside the final furlong, allowing Silver Ghost or Mudbir to sweep past.
scenarios.body: If the early tempo is just quick enough that Northern Express ties up inside the final furlong, allowing Silver Ghost or Mudbir to sweep past.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Express burns up the early fractions under pressure from a crowded prominent group, leaving daylight for a genuine closer to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: If Northern Express burns up the early fractions under pressure from a crowded prominent group, leaving daylight for a genuine closer to finish powerfully.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Squeeze Produces Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes congested in a tight-knit pack and a redistributed horse, forced off its natural pattern, nonetheless finds a lucky run to challenge.
scenarios.body: If the race becomes congested in a tight-knit pack and a redistributed horse, forced off its natural pattern, nonetheless finds a lucky run to challenge.

watchPoints.text: Northern Express — if he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged he will be very hard to reel in on this flat, Good Newmarket straight; watch whether any prominent horse makes a genuine bid to go with him in the first two furlongs, as that is the only thing likely to unsettle his rhythm.

Silver Ghost — Cieren Fallon is adept at tracking a lone front-runner and delivering a clean two-furlong challenge; if he slots in behind Northern Express in second without being crowded out by the other prominent types, he becomes the most dangerous challenger in the race.

Mudbir and Philanthropist — both are prominent types competing for the same early real estate; if they bump or impede each other exiting the stalls, one or both may be forced to race in an uncharacteristic position and their chances will be materially affected.

Darkness and Dark Tornado — both visor-wearing hold-up horses with strong recent good-ground profiles, but the controlled single-pace scenario this race is likely to produce is the one shape that least suits a sustained late run; monitor them only if post-race sectionals suggest the early pace was faster than expected.

Nostrum — watch his starting position in the stalls and how quickly Rawlinson moves him up; if he is able to slot into a midfield tracking position without expending early energy, his placed 7f form gives him an outside chance, but any awkward beginning will effectively end his participation.

races.name: hnwines.co.uk Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Crystal Pier
runners_data.note: Won last time at 8f on Good for Beckett and Rossa Ryan — a powerful combination — and her hold-up style is genuine, meaning she needs a strong enough tempo to get involved; the expected steady gallop set by Silent City is her chief concern here.

runners_data.name: Darzah
runners_data.note: Haggas-trained at OR 78 with a win on Firm suggesting she handles fast ground well, but her sole Good-ground runs show a single eighth-place finish at this trip; Cieren Fallon will look to slot in just behind the leader and hope the form turns around on this surface.

runners_data.name: Luna Celeste
runners_data.note: Three runs, two placings and a win at 6f on Good — stepping up markedly to a mile is the big unknown — but Tom Clover has her in form (LR 31d) and Saffie Osborne rides a prominent style that suits the expected race shape well.

runners_data.name: Come On Eibhlin
runners_data.note: Dylan Egan's mount is a true hold-up filly whose recent form (5-4633) has been ordinary at distances shorter than today's mile, and while the extra furlong may suit, her natural style means she will struggle to get the rear position she wants in this seven-runner field — the compressed pace is likely to find her racing closer than ideal.

runners_data.name: Thursday Girl
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — no tactical relevance; flagged for information only and should be excluded from any assessment of the race shape.

runners_data.name: Silent City
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's lightly-raced three-year-old carries the top weight (144lbs) and a strong Newmarket record (2W, 5P in 6 Good-ground starts) but has not run for 246 days; the layoff is the key risk to what is otherwise the dominant tactical force in this race, and the STYLE_FIT flag reminds us her role as lone front-runner is slightly out of her usual pattern.

runners_data.name: Bridget's View
runners_data.note: A four-year-old whose last five runs all returned finishes of fifth or worse, including three consecutive last-two placings on Good ground; OR 82 looks hard to exploit on current form, and the Olivia Haines 7lb claim does not fully compensate for a trainer (Williams, T14: 1/8) who is out of form.

races.paceDynamic: Silent City is the lone confirmed front-runner and, coming off a 246-day absence, will likely be allowed to bowl along at a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the Newmarket mile's Rowley Mile start. Darzah and Luna Celeste will press forward to dispute second and third, but neither has the profile to seriously challenge for the lead, meaning Silent City controls tempo entirely. The resulting shape — a single horse dictating a steady-to-moderate pace with a small prominent group tucked just behind — will compress the race into a short-run finale, suiting those who can travel smoothly in the first half and quicken off the pace in the closing two furlongs. This race shape strongly favours the prominent and mid-division profiles over genuine hold-up horses; the field contains more closers than the map can place at the rear, with Come On Eibhlin a true hold-up type displaced forward into a midfield slot she is unlikely to naturally occupy.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Silent City Controls Easily
scenarios.trigger: If Silent City bowls along uncontested and the pace stays honest without acceleration until the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Silent City bowls along uncontested and the pace stays honest without acceleration until the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Silent City's long absence blunts her finishing kick and one of the prominent horses pounces in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Silent City's long absence blunts her finishing kick and one of the prominent horses pounces in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and a late gap opens for a hold-up finisher coming from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses in the straight and a late gap opens for a hold-up finisher coming from off the bridle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Break Scrambles Order
scenarios.trigger: If the start is unruly, multiple horses contest the lead aggressively and the race devolves into a muddling gallop.
scenarios.body: If the start is unruly, multiple horses contest the lead aggressively and the race devolves into a muddling gallop.

watchPoints.text: Silent City's 246-day layoff is the single biggest danger sign in the race — if she returns below peak fitness, the entire dominant scenario collapses and Darzah or Luna Celeste inherit a race they would otherwise not control.

Luna Celeste has never run beyond 6f — watch whether she stays the mile trip, as any sign of tiring inside the final two furlongs would confirm the trip is beyond her current scope despite good recent form.

Come On Eibhlin is a genuine hold-up type who will be forced to race closer to the pace than she wants in a seven-runner field; if she does get bumped forward early, watch whether jockey D Egan allows her to settle or is forced to commit too soon.

Bridget's View has shown zero improvement across her last five Good-ground runs and is worth monitoring purely to see whether the step back to 8f and the 7lb claim from Haines produces any sign of her returning to form — if she travels easily midrace, it would be an early danger signal for the leaders.

With Thursday Girl a non-runner, the field drops to six effective runners — confirm market moves on Silent City and Crystal Pier in the final hour as any significant support would reinforce the dominant pace scenario.
